items.title: Death outside Vancouver Island hospital raises questions about rural emergency care access
items.summary_auto: The death of a person outside the Port Hardy Hospital on northern Vancouver Island has renewed concerns about access to emergency care in rural B.C., where staffing shortages have forced some hospitals to close their emergency departments overnight.

items.title: City of Regina plans to shut down public transit starting Monday
items.summary_auto: ATU Canada president said workers have not had a new collective agreement for almost two years and the city chose to suspend services after the union said it would implement a ban on voluntary overtime starting Monday.

items.title: Cavalry FC defeats Atlético Ottawa 3-2 to claim CPL title and historic double
items.summary_auto: Cavalry FC defeated Atlético Ottawa 3-2 to claim the Canadian Premier League title and an unprecedented double in the soccer league.

items.title: Becky Druhan wins N.S. Liberal leadership, becomes first woman to lead party
items.summary_auto: Becky Druhan has defeated Amanda Mombourquette in a two-person race to become the first female leader of the Nova Scotia Liberals.

items.title: Ontario Liberals elect Navdeep Bains as new party leader
items.summary_auto: Ontario Liberals have elected Navdeep Bains as the party's new leader after a marathon nine-month leadership race, with Bains emerging as victor less than one percentage point ahead of his next closest competitor, provincial caucus member Lee Fairclough.

items.title: UN talks on AI in warfare end with no commitment to binding rules
items.summary_auto: UN-backed talks this week on regulating AI in warfare ended Saturday with nations agreeing to further discussion, but without a consensus on developing firm rules on how to rein in deadly autonomous weapons.

items.title: Etsy faces backlash over including AI model training in new policy update
items.summary_auto: Some Etsy sellers across Canada are removing products from the platform amid criticism for introducing AI model training as part of a policy change.

items.title: FBI investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
items.summary_auto: The FBI is investigating a reported breach of its criminal information database, according to U.S. media reports. This is the second time the FBI has been the target of a cyberattack since September.

items.title: Montreal police arrest 2 ex-officers for alleged assault, criminal harassment, breach of trust
items.summary_auto: The two officers had previously been placed on administrative leave and then fired from the Montreal police service. They were arrested after Quebec's Crown prosecutor's office issued a warrant.

items.title: Capture of cartel leader in northern Mexico sets off gunfight that leaves 11 dead
items.summary_auto: A burst of violence in Mexico's Sinaloa state after authorities captured cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro, left at least 11 people dead, authorities said Saturday.

items.title: Israeli strike kills 3 in vehicle distributing aid in Gaza, witnesses say
items.summary_auto: Israeli forces on Saturday hit a truck in Gaza, which witnesses said was carrying food and papers bearing the ‌logo of the World Central Kitchen charity, but the organization said the vehicle was not affiliated with it.

items.title: Russian strike on Zelenskyy's hometown in central Ukraine kills 2, wounds 60
items.summary_auto: A Russian strike on the centre of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown, Kryvyi Rih, killed two people and wounded 60 others, local officials said Saturday.

items.title: A real '3 Body Problem': Astronomers discover a nearby 'weirdo' triple-star system
items.summary_auto: An international team of astronomers led by the University of Montreal has found a nearby triple-star system, much like the one in the Netflix show 3 Body Problem. But this one seems to be… a little odd.

items.title: Hearing on controversial plans to export power from Powell River to U.S. wraps up
items.summary_auto: An unprecedented federal hearing for an independent power producer's application to export all its electricity from a small B.C. community to the U.S. for 30 years wrapped up on Friday, after arguments from the company and local intervenors opposed to the deal.

items.title: 'We are sorry': Rocks found in restaurant burritos in Alberta
items.summary_auto: BarBurrito issued an apology to its customers after pea-sized stones were found in some of its burritos at restaurants in Alberta. The company says the rocks came from a particular brand of beans that it is no longer using.

items.title: Age-Friendly initiative works to help Sask. seniors stay in their home communities
items.summary_auto: A program started by the World Health Organization is now developing in 16 locations across the province. Each community forms a committee that follows a template designed to address gaps in services available to older adults.

items.title: Satellites are constantly photographing Earth. A Waterloo student has compiled the pictures into one spot
items.summary_auto: Satellites are constantly photographing Earth, and a new website designed by a University of Waterloo student is making these public photos more accessible to the general public.

items.title: Woman's airport security ordeal with dad's ashes highlights challenges of travelling with cremated remains
items.summary_auto: Rules around transporting creamated remains through airports and challenges with new scanners can add "another layer of grief" to an already stressful time, says the head of the Funeral Service Association of Canada.

items.title: Judge awards damages to both sides in lawsuit after neighbours' dispute over loose dogs 'spun out of control'
items.summary_auto: A judge has awarded an eastern Manitoba couple sued by their neighbour $10,000 in damages, and their neighbour $1,000, after an "unfortunate series of events" unfolded over dogs allowed to run loose on an unfenced property.

items.title: Mild months ahead: What we know about this winter across southern Ontario
items.summary_auto: Historically, the average high on Nov. 19 has been around 7.5 C in Toronto, so the weather outside is noticeably warmer. That's welcome news to those who fear the cold, but should we be concerned?

items.title: N.B. publisher of Giller Prize-winning novel says win proves important stories can come out of the Maritimes
items.summary_auto: Susanne Alexander, the publisher at Goose Lane Editions, said Nicholas Herring was a dark horse in the running for the Giller Prize. When he won, she was ecstatic.

items.title: Rohingya 'clearance operation' survivor in N.L. triumphant following genocide ruling
items.summary_auto: Muhammad Rofique of St. John's is celebrating, but still reflecting upon the atrocities he lived through in Myanmar as the world’s highest court declares the country committed genocide against his people.

items.title: The pros, cons and risks of using AI as your personal assistant
A Canadian study pinned a baby's death on codeine passed through breast milk. 20 years on, it's been retracted
items.summary_auto: A highly influential yet controversial Canadian study that linked a baby's death to codeine passed through breastmilk — and informed global guidance on breastfeeding and pain management over the last two decades — has been pulled from a leading medical journal, which said omissions in the research amounted to "falsification."

items.title: Israeli settler violence at unprecedented levels during Palestinian olive harvest
items.summary_auto: There have been more settler attacks against Palestinians and their property during this year’s olive harvest than in 20 years of record-keeping by the United Nations.

items.title: Allies are buying Canadian underwater surveillance drones. Canada is 'not there yet'
items.summary_auto: Canada has a three-ocean coastline — 243,000 kilometres — and only 20 underwater drones to help defend it. The navy's commander confirms there isn't a solution ready a year after an internal document shows top officials talked about the need for a short-term fix.

items.title: Elon Musk looks to break up with MAGA. To what end?
items.summary_auto: Elon Musk has certainly seemed to embrace the Make America Great Again movement. Why does that matter? Because the Tesla and Space X CEO now appears to be distancing himself.

items.title: Canada's first climate lawsuit to go to trial has wrapped up hearings. Many more are underway
items.summary_auto: What level of responsibility does the federal government bear for the climate disasters Canadians are suffering? That's the question at the heart of a landmark lawsuit that wrapped up witness testimony in Federal Court in Vancouver on Friday, and whose outcome could have a big influence on how a growing number of other climate lawsuits in Canada pan out.

items.title: Lawyers appeal nearly $500M cut to fees in historic $10B Robinson Huron Treaty settlement
items.summary_auto: Ontario’s top court heard an appeal Friday by the legal team behind the $10-billion Robinson Huron Treaty settlement — challenging a judge’s decision to slash their legal fees by nearly half a billion dollars.

items.title: Tips are off the table at this Montreal café — and customers are into it
items.summary_auto: Café 5thFloor in the city’s LaSalle borough doesn’t take tips. Instead it pays its workers a livable wage. If customers are compelled to tip, the coffee shop takes donations that go to the non-profit, Centraide.

items.title: How Canadian Survivor contestant Daniel Kilby lost most of his belongings to auction after filming the show
items.summary_auto: Canadian Survivor contestant Daniel Kilby lost many of his personal belongings earlier this year, including a painting of a "cheetah dressed as a general," his PlayStation 5 and many household appliances, after missed payments on a storage locker while he was on the show led to his belongings being put up for auction.
